exposure: duration of term prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM) (<12 hours vs. 12-18 hours)
cohort: The study included 6,828 patients with singleton term prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM) lasting less than 18 hours, without fetal anomalies or incomplete medical records.
finding: Term prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM) lasting 12-18 hours was associated with significantly higher rates of maternal (clinical chorioamnionitis, intrapartum fever) and neonatal infections (NICU admission, sepsis workups, NICU antibiotic treatment) compared to PROM lasting <12 hours.
mod_finding: PROM lasting 12-18 hours was associated with a lower frequency of vaginal delivery and higher rates of cesarean and vacuum-assisted delivery compared to PROM lasting <12 hours.
followup_time: N/A (lack of long-term maternal and neonatal follow-up)
